signature.instructions:
You are given the raw text of a political fundraising email. Identify the political committee that sponsored (paid for) the email.

Domain knowledge: U.S. political fundraising emails are legally required to carry a disclaimer naming the paying committee, usually near the very bottom, worded like 'Paid for by <COMMITTEE NAME>' or 'Paid for and authorized by <COMMITTEE NAME>', often followed by 'and not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee', a mailing address, a website, and unsubscribe text. The committee name is also frequently repeated immediately afterwards in the footer sender/address block (so the same name can appear twice back-to-back, sometimes with no space between the copies), or in the sending domain, or in a line like 'Contributions or gifts to <NAME> are not tax deductible' or 'to stop receiving emails from <NAME>'.

Rules:
- Return the committee's name exactly as printed in the disclaimer, in normal mixed-case form (if the disclaimer is ALL CAPS but the same name appears elsewhere in mixed case, use the mixed-case spelling).
- If the name appears twice in a row, return it only ONCE.
- Committee names may legitimately contain small numerals or digits-as-words (e.g. a number standing for a district, a state, or an election year). Keep those digits; they are part of the name. Do NOT keep street numbers, PO Box numbers, ZIP codes, or phone numbers.
- Drop a grammatical article that merely introduces the name: 'Paid for by the <NAME>' means the committee is '<NAME>', without 'the'. Only keep a leading 'The' when it is clearly part of the registered name (capitalized and used that way elsewhere).
- If the disclaimer names the committee by its acronym/initialism, return that acronym in capital letters exactly as printed; do NOT expand it into the long form, and do not invent a long form.
- Keep words like Fund, Committee, PAC, Party, Victory, Action, 'for Congress', 'for Senate' that are part of the name.
- Exclude street address, PO Box, city/state/ZIP, phone numbers, URLs, 'not authorized by any candidate...' language, 'a joint fundraising committee composed of...' explanations, and any trailing punctuation.
- Do NOT return a candidate's bare personal name unless that literally is the committee name; do not abbreviate or reword a name that is not in the text.
- The email text may have words glued together by line wrapping; restore normal spacing.
- Output only the committee name, nothing else.
